groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Kiri was on a trip to Cambodia with his granddaughter, Sophea. After months of planning, their dream was finally __(16: realised)__ as they travelled to Kampong Thom, where he grew up. __(17: Entranced)__ by the beautiful fields and the distant clamour of roosters crowing, Sophea walked to the river where her grandfather had once spent hours fishing.
The duo trekked __(18: laboriously)__ up the hill, perspiration dotting their brows. They could see the vast countryside stretching before them from the summit. The view mirrored __(19: to a great extent)__ the stories Kiri had told her of his childhood — untouched, vivid, and full of quiet wonder. Kiri was confident that although time had passed, the bond he shared with Sophea would __(20: stand the test of time)__ with each cherished memory. This trip would be etched in their hearts and minds forever.

Study the poster (Text 1) and the extract from a school talk (Text 2) and answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 1++
The text below shows a poster for an event.
[[img1]]
++Text 2++
The extract below is taken from a school talk.
A strong community makes us feel safe and connected, and it all begins at home. The family serves as the foundation of a healthy support system and spending quality time together lays the groundwork for overcoming life's challenges.
Family time offers invaluable benefits: it strengthens emotional bonds, boosts confidence, and reinforces our sense of self-worth. For children, it cultivates a robust sense of identity, helping them grow into confident and secure adults.
There are countless ways to enjoy quality family time. Indoors, a lively game night can fill the house with laughter and joy. Outdoors, a simple picnic in the park can create cherished memories while allowing us to admire nature.
As the saying goes, "Home is where the heart is." When family bonds are strong, they form the heart of a thriving community. Together, we support and uplift one another. In this way, we grow stronger.

There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ONCE.**
[[table1]]

Within the Singapore Botanic Gardens stands a living landmark of national pride. Native __(26)__ Singapore, the Tembusu Tree can grow up to 40 metres tall. Its most distinctive feature – a gently curled, low-hanging branch – reaches outward as if offering a reminder of its presence to __(27)__ who walk past. Also known affectionately as the "Five-dollar Tree", this is the tree that graces the back of the note. Few would expect such __(28)__ iconic image to be not only real but also __(29)__ accessible to the public. The image is so ingrained in our everyday life that people often overlook the significance __(30)__ the symbol.
This heritage tree is believed to have existed __(31)__ the Botanic Gardens was officially founded in 1859. Close to two centuries old, this tree __(32)__ been admired by generations, some of whom return just to marvel at its resilience. __(33)__ its thick, weathered trunk and an expansive canopy of branches, the tree represents the enduring spirit of a nation. Standing unshaken by storms __(34)__ remaining deeply grounded in its values, it never forsakes the roots that define it. The Tembusu Tree is truly a symbol of what Singapore takes pride in – __(35)__ anchored and forward-looking. Such is the spirit of the country.

The Museum of Toys is nestled in the heart of our city. Driven by his passion for design and art, Marcus, an enthusiastic toy __(46)__, often imagined a space where visitors from all __(47)__ of life could rediscover the past, and rekindle childhood memories of playing with favourite figurines and stuffed toys. His dream finally came true in 2007 when he successfully set up this museum, __(48)__ his personal collection from more than forty countries.

Read the passage and answer questions 66 to 75.

**1** Creak... The closet door groaned in protest as I tugged it open, its hinges squealing like they, too, wanted no part in what lay inside. Hanging limply before me was a rabbit costume – not the soft, storybook kind, but a garish ensemble of neon pink fur with ears that drooped like they had given up hope. Its oversized head sagged to one side. My heart sank. This was it. My debut performance. My graduation day. A room with an expectant audience... and that was what I had to wear? Taking in the **scene**, I noticed the others – fluffy sheep, dignified goats, even cows that looked halfway decent. Somehow, everyone's outfit looked far more presentable than mine. There and then, I had the urge to slip away.
**2** "Where are you going, Gary?" Leon's voice stopped me. He was fiddling with the long frayed tail of his goat costume, looking as ridiculous as I felt, yet standing tall all the same. He gave a look – the kind that only best friends would, halfway between challenge and comfort. "It's okay to be nervous," he said, his voice filled with quiet determination. "We all start somewhere. You've put in blood, sweat and tears for this. You're not backing out now, are you? We're all in this together." His words hit me. The long rehearsals, the endless retakes, the body aches. Had I forgotten all **those**? I took a deep breath. Not for the costumes but the effort. Not for the pink rabbit but for the people who believed in me. I was not going to run away. Not this time.
**3** Two days later at the full-dress rehearsal, my confidence cracked. The auditorium was buzzing with quiet chatter. My silly costume made every movement a chore; each hop felt unnatural, blown out of proportion. I shuffled out, my heart pounding like a drum. The spotlight lit the stage as if it were preparing to expose my secret. I began my scene. Then came the giggles. Small at first, then spreading like wildfire. My shoulders slumped when I stumbled over a line. Laughter. More laughter. The gnawing doubt clawed at me – was that failure? What a disaster! If there were a trapdoor, I would gladly vanish. Exiting the stage after my part, my oversized foot caught on a mess of wires. Like a puppet with its strings cut, I tripped and landed on my knees. Laughter exploded. **Lying there, humiliation scorched my face.** All of a sudden, something changed. I remembered Leon's words. "We all start somewhere." I knew I had to face my fears. Slowly, the nerves faded away.
**4** Then came the opening night. The curtain rose to thunderous applause. My stomach churned with butterflies, but this time, I welcomed them. As I hopped into the spotlight, the audience erupted into laughter – not mockery, but delight. Every exaggerated movement, every silly twitch of my ears added to the joy. I was not being laughed at. Instead, my antics were making the guests laugh. Backstage, Leon flashed me a thumbs-up. The fears were irrational. I had made peace with them.
**5** "See? You did it! You're a natural," he said when the final applause rang out. I smiled, the joy of the moment finally sinking in.
**6** "Thanks for talking me out of leaving. **It** isn't so bad after all," I replied, tugging at the floppy ears. "This outfit still looks ridiculous." Leon grinned. In that pink fluff, I had learnt about courage and that the stage was not about perfection. It was about showing up, even when I was scared. My debut performance was a success.

questions.stem:
Part 1: Situational Writing (14 marks)
The pictures below show a student and a librarian at Westview Library. Study the pictures carefully.
[[img1]]
++Your Task++
Imagine you are William Wong.
**Write an email to the Manager of Westview Library to commend his staff for the excellent service.**
You are to refer to the pictures and information above for your email. The bullet point underlined below requires you to come up with your own information.
In your email, include the following key information:
• the date of your visit
• the name of the staff member and how she helped you
• other than being helpful, give one other commendable quality she possesses
• what you like the most about the reading corner
• ++one suggestion you have for the reading corner++
You may reorder the points. Remember to write in complete sentences.

images.alt: Four comic panels at Westview Library. Panel 1 (caption: 18 February 2025, 2.00 p.m.): the librarian hands William a book over the counter. Librarian: "Here you go, William. I found a copy of the poetry book you've been looking for at Lagoon Library and asked them to transfer it here as soon as possible. I know you need this urgently." William: "Thanks, Miss Lim. Now I can start on my project. It's due in two days' time." Panel 2: they are at a bookshelf and an armchair under a sign 'Reading Corner'. Miss Lim: "By the way, what do you think of our reading corner? It's been quite a while since we refreshed it and it could do with a new look. Do you have any ideas to make it more conducive?" William: "Well, it's rather comfortable. Nothing beats reading at this quiet little space where I can immerse myself in the world of books." Panel 3: William says, "Anyway, I'm excited about the revamp and will give it some thought. I'll get back to you with my suggestion." Panel 4: William thinks, "Librarians like Miss Lim are hard to come by. I'll write an email to commend her and also share a suggestion for the reading corner."

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Purpose: to commend (praise) a staff member for excellent service, and to share a suggestion for the reading corner. Say this clearly in the opening lines.

Audience: the Manager of Westview Library, an adult you do not know. Use a formal, polite tone: 'Dear Sir' or 'Dear Manager', no contractions, slang or emojis, and end with 'Yours faithfully' or 'Yours sincerely' and your full name, William Wong.
Context: you are William Wong, a student who visited the library and was helped by the librarian.
Point 1, the date of your visit: 18 February 2025.

Point 2, the name of the staff member and how she helped you: Miss Lim found a copy of the poetry book you had been looking for at Lagoon Library and asked for it to be transferred to Westview Library as soon as possible (because she knew you needed it urgently).

Point 3, one other commendable quality besides being helpful: infer it from the pictures, for example thoughtful or considerate (she knew you needed the book urgently), proactive or resourceful (she searched another library), or open to feedback (she asked for your ideas). Do not write 'helpful' again.
Point 4, what you like most about the reading corner: it is comfortable, a quiet little space where you can immerse yourself in the world of books.

Point 5 (underlined, your own idea), one suggestion for the reading corner: it must be sensible and make the corner more conducive, for example adding brighter reading lamps, more cushions or beanbags, a display shelf of recommended books, or plants.

Format and language: a subject line, short paragraphs, complete sentences and correct tenses (past tense for the visit, present tense for your opinion and suggestion). Close by thanking the Manager. 6 marks are for covering the task and 8 marks for language and organisation.

review.keyAnswer: No model answer in the key.
review.solvedAnswer: Checklist written from the task box and the pictures.
review.note: In the PDF the Paper 1 pages are split: the pictures are on page 2 and the task box is on page 13, after the listening paper. The stem says 'the pictures and information above' where the paper says 'on page 2'.

questions.stem:
Part 2: Continuous Writing (36 marks)
Write a composition of ++at least 150 words++ about **an unexpected delivery**.
The pictures are provided to help you think about this topic.
Your composition must be based on at least one of these pictures.
[[img1]]
Consider the following points when you plan your composition:
• What was the delivery?
• Why was it unexpected?
You may use the points in any order and include other relevant points as well.

images.alt: Three pictures. Picture 1: a sealed cardboard box labelled 'HANDLE WITH CARE'. Picture 2: a handwritten letter sticking out of an opened envelope. Picture 3: two tickets, each printed 'ENTRY TICKET'.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Understand the topic: a delivery is something brought or sent to someone. 'Unexpected' means nobody saw it coming: it was not ordered, it came from a surprising sender, it arrived at a strange time, or what was inside was a surprise. Both words must drive the story.

Picture 1 (box marked 'Handle with care'): a parcel nobody ordered arrives at the door. It could hold something fragile or even alive, a gift from a relative overseas, or a parcel meant for a neighbour.
Picture 2 (letter in an envelope): a letter arrives from someone you had lost touch with, such as an old friend, a former teacher or a grandparent, bringing news, an apology or thanks.
Picture 3 (entry tickets): tickets to a concert, match or theme park turn up, perhaps a prize you forgot you entered for, or a secret treat from a parent to reward your hard work.
Answer the two guiding points clearly: what the delivery was, and why it was unexpected. Use at least one picture; you may combine them (a box that holds a letter and two tickets).

Story arc: an ordinary day, the doorbell rings or the postman arrives (build curiosity), opening the delivery, the problem or surprise it brings (whose is it? should you keep it? who sent it?), the turning point, and how it is resolved.
Show feelings with actions and thoughts (puzzled, suspicious, thrilled, touched) and include some dialogue.

Ending: return to the topic. Reflect on what the unexpected delivery taught you or how it changed something, for example gratitude for someone who remembered you, or honesty in returning what was not yours.
Write at least 150 words (aim for 350 to 450) in paragraphs. 18 marks are for content and 18 for language and organisation.

review.keyAnswer: No model answer in the key.
review.solvedAnswer: Planning checklist written from the topic and pictures.

questions.stem: The jury __________ unable to reach a verdict due to the fact that they had different opinions.

explanation: Tense: 'they **had** different opinions' is in the past, so the missing verb must be past tense. That rules out 'is' and 'are'.
'jury' is a collective noun. When the members act together as one unit it is singular; when they act as separate people it is plural.
Here the members had different opinions, and the sentence calls them 'they'. They are acting as individuals, so the verb is plural.
'The jury were unable to reach a verdict.' The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Mei Ling, along with her uncle, __________ chess regularly since she developed a love for the game.

explanation: 'since she developed a love for the game' tells us the action started in the past and is still going on. 'since' needs a perfect tense, so 'plays' and 'is playing' are out.
'regularly' shows a repeated, continuing activity. The present perfect continuous (has been + verb-ing) stresses that it has kept going up to now, so it fits better than 'has played'.
Agreement: the subject is 'Mei Ling'. 'along with her uncle' is only extra information between commas, so the verb stays singular: 'has'.
'Mei Ling ... has been playing chess regularly since ...' The answer is option (4).

review.note: 'has played' (option 3) is also grammatical with 'since'. Option (4) is the best answer because 'regularly' points to an ongoing, repeated activity.

questions.stem: Mrs Rai looked on with pride as her son delivered a speech that he had prepared by __________.

explanation: 'by + reflexive pronoun' means alone, without help.
The reflexive pronoun must match the person who did the action. Who prepared the speech? 'he', Mrs Rai's son.
The reflexive pronoun for 'he' is 'himself'. 'herself' is the trap because Mrs Rai is mentioned first, but she did not prepare the speech.
The answer is option (2), himself.

questions.stem: "Emily never forgets to remind her grandmother to take her medicine, __________?" remarked Mother.

explanation: Rule: a positive statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes a positive tag.
'never' makes the statement negative, even though there is no 'not'. So the tag must be positive. That rules out 'isn't she' and 'doesn't she'.
The verb 'forgets' is simple present, so the helping verb in the tag is 'does', not 'will'.
'Emily never forgets ..., does she?' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: "Attend to the guests promptly __________ they need assistance," the restaurant manager reminded his staff during his briefing.

explanation: The blank joins an instruction to a condition: attend to the guests **if** they need assistance.
In formal English, 'should' can replace 'if' when the helping verb comes before the subject: 'should they need assistance' = 'if they should need assistance'.
'shall', 'must' and 'could' cannot be used in this way to mean 'if'.
The answer is option (4), should.

questions.stem: The Long Island Project is by far __________ scheme to combat rising sea levels along Singapore's coastline.

explanation: 'by far' means 'by a great amount'. It is used to strengthen a superlative: by far the best, by far the largest.
The superlative of 'significant' is 'the most significant'.
'a more significant' is a comparative and would need 'than ...' after it. 'the very significant' is not a superlative.
The answer is option (4), the most significant.

questions.stem: The government introduced electric buses __________ the high costs as they were committed to a greener public transport system.

explanation: Work out how the two ideas are linked. High costs are a reason **not** to introduce electric buses, yet the government did it anyway. That is a contrast.
'in spite of + noun' shows contrast: something happened even though there was an obstacle.

'owing to', 'because of' and 'resulting from' all give a cause. The buses were not introduced because of the high costs; the real reason comes later ('as they were committed to a greener ... system').
The answer is option (2), in spite of.

questions.stem: The tour guide, __________ company had conducted the Angkor Wat historical tour, has received excellent reviews.

explanation: The blank is followed by a noun, 'company'. The company belongs to the tour guide.
'whose' is the relative pronoun that shows possession: the tour guide's company = whose company.
'who' is tempting because the tour guide is a person, but 'who company had conducted' is not grammatical. 'who' must be followed by a verb, not a noun that belongs to the person.
The answer is option (4), whose.

questions.stem: If you have plans to visit this modern city, be sure to put __________ at least two hours for a complete experience.

explanation: 'put aside' (also 'set aside') means to save or reserve time or money for a purpose.
'put away' means to keep something in its proper place. 'put behind' means to forget something unpleasant. 'put across' means to explain an idea clearly.
You reserve two hours for the visit, so 'put aside at least two hours' is correct.
The answer is option (2), aside.

questions.stem: There is __________ doubt that Janice will win the award given her outstanding performance.

explanation: 'doubt' is an uncountable noun here, so 'few' (used with countable plural nouns) is wrong.
Meaning: her performance was outstanding, so people are almost sure she will win. There is hardly any doubt.

'little' means 'almost no' and goes with uncountable nouns: 'There is little doubt that ...' is a fixed expression. 'much doubt' gives the opposite meaning, and 'any' needs a negative ('There isn't any doubt').
The answer is option (3), little.

questions.stem: When the tsunami warning alarm went off, residents were told to __________ the area immediately and head for higher ground.

explanation: Clues: a tsunami warning, 'immediately' and 'head for higher ground'. People must leave a dangerous place for safety.
'evacuate' means to leave a place because it is dangerous. We say 'evacuate the area'.
'depart' also means to leave, but it is used for ordinary journeys and needs 'from' (depart from the area). 'survey' and 'observe' mean to look at something carefully.
The answer is option (4), evacuate.

questions.stem: Many tourists are unaware of the __________ effects their visits can have on the heritage sites. A number have suffered irreparable damage.

explanation: Clue in the second sentence: 'irreparable damage' is damage that can never be repaired. The effects are extremely harmful.
'devastating' means causing very great damage or destruction.

'subtle' means hard to notice, which is tempting because the tourists are 'unaware', but it does not match damage that is beyond repair. 'temporary' (lasting a short time) is the opposite of irreparable.
The answer is option (4), devastating.

questions.stem: The lack of proper shelter during heavy rain has become a major __________ for the school community.

explanation: Not having shelter in heavy rain is a problem that worries people in the school.
'concern' means a matter that causes worry. 'a major concern for ...' is a common word pair.
'lapse' is a small mistake or slip. 'obstruction' is something that blocks the way, and 'interference' is unwanted meddling. A lack of shelter is none of these.
The answer is option (2), concern.

questions.stem: My little nephew __________ when he saw blood trickling down his grazed knee.

explanation: Some people faint at the sight of blood. 'passed out' means fainted, or lost consciousness.
'passed up' means chose not to take (a chance). 'passed off' means pretended that something was something else. 'passed over' means ignored or not chosen.
Only 'passed out' can stand alone without an object and fits the sight of blood.
The answer is option (3), passed out.

questions.stem: The students were hesitant to speak __________ in front of the discipline master for fear of being reprimanded.

explanation: Clue: 'for fear of being reprimanded' (scolded). The students were afraid that telling the truth openly would get them into trouble.
'candidly' means honestly and openly, without hiding anything.
'tactfully' means carefully, so as not to upset anyone. Nobody is scolded for speaking tactfully, so there would be nothing to fear. 'deliberately' means on purpose, and 'eagerly' means keenly.
The answer is option (3), candidly.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++realised++.

explanation: When a dream is 'realised', it becomes real: it comes true.
Clue: 'After months of planning, their dream was finally realised as they travelled to Kampong Thom'. The trip they dreamed of actually happened.
'materialised' means became real or actually happened, which matches.
'revealed' means made known, and 'manifested' means shown clearly. The dream was not shown to anyone; it came true. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++Entranced++.

explanation: 'Entranced' means filled with such wonder and delight that you give something all your attention, as if in a trance.
Clue: Sophea was entranced 'by the beautiful fields and the distant clamour of roosters crowing'. The scenery held her attention.
'Captivated' means attracted and held by something charming, which matches.
'Gratified' means pleased or satisfied, which is weaker and does not carry the idea of being spellbound. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++laboriously++.

explanation: 'laboriously' means with a lot of effort and difficulty ('labour' means hard work).
Clue: 'perspiration dotting their brows'. The climb up the hill was hard work.
'strenuously' means with great effort and energy, which matches.
'tirelessly' is the trap: it means without getting tired, but they were clearly straining. 'hastily' means in a hurry. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++to a great extent++.

explanation: 'to a great extent' means mostly, or in large part, but not completely.
The view matched the stories Kiri had told for the most part.
'mainly' means mostly, which matches.
'purely' means completely and only, which is too strong: 'a great extent' is not the whole. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++stand the test of time++.

explanation: The idiom 'stand the test of time' means to stay strong or good for a very long time.
Kiri was confident that his bond with Sophea 'would stand the test of time', that is, it would last.
'sustain' needs an object (to sustain something), so 'the bond would sustain' does not work. 'deepen' means to become stronger, which is a different idea from continuing for a long time.
The key's answer is option (1), last. 'endure' (option 2) has almost the same meaning; see the note.

review.note: The key gives (1) last. Solving it independently, (2) endure fits just as well: 'the bond would endure' and 'the bond would last' both mean it would stand the test of time, and dictionaries define the idiom with both words. The stored answer follows the key, but a child who chooses (2) has not made a real mistake. A parent may want to check with the school's own answer.

questions.stem: According to the poster in Text 1, the movie __________.
options: stars Leo Graham and Felicity Vale

explanation: Check each option against the poster.
The poster says 'Based on a true story by Felicity Vale.' A film based on a true story is inspired by true events, so (2) is correct.

(1) Willow Park is the venue where the film is shown, not what the film is about. (3) Elliot Drake **produced** the film; the poster does not say he directed it. (4) Felicity Vale wrote the story; she is not one of the three actors listed.
The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Based on the poster in Text 1, which of the following **best** fits the film that will be screened in the park?

explanation: Look at the tagline and the picture: 'An abandoned manor in the woods... Many mysteries to unravel... With every step deeper, the danger closes in... Will he escape?'
Mystery, danger and suspense are the marks of a thriller. The dark, spooky manor in the picture supports this.
'Documentary' is tempting because the film is 'based on a true story', but it has actors playing characters ('Leo Graham as Jamie'), so it is not a documentary. Nothing suggests cartoons or science.
The answer is option (1), Thriller.

questions.stem: "Many mysteries to unravel... Will he escape?" The image in the poster **best** supports this by giving the impression that the boy is __________.

explanation: Look at the image on the screen: a small figure stands alone, upright, facing a huge dark manor at night.
The tagline calls him 'One brave boy' who goes 'deeper' even as 'the danger closes in'. Standing squarely in front of the frightening manor shows he is ready to go in.
That gives the impression he is determined and fearless. He is not 'relaxed' (there is danger), and nothing shows him as bored, confused or hesitant.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: "Ready for a magical night under the stars with your loved ones?" Why did the writer ask the question in Text 1?
options: to spark people's interest in magic
to make people connect with the movie
to invite people to join Willow Film Club
to encourage people to attend the movie screening

explanation: The question speaks directly to the reader ('your loved ones') and describes the event: a night outdoors 'under the stars'.
A question like this at the top of a poster is a hook. It makes readers picture themselves enjoying the evening so that they will want to come.

(1) 'magical' here means wonderful, not about magic tricks. (2) The question is about the outdoor event, not the film's story. (3) The poster asks people to register for the event, not to join the club.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Text 2 supports the message of the poster in Text 1 as it also __________.
options: encourages people to have more picnics
focusses on the need to build a strong community
highlights spending fruitful time with family members

explanation: Find what the two texts share. The poster invites people to enjoy a night 'with your loved ones'. Text 2 is about 'spending quality time together' as a family and its benefits.
So both texts are about spending meaningful time with family. 'fruitful time' means the same as 'quality time'.
(3) is the trap: Text 2 does mention a strong community, but the poster does not, so it is not something the texts share. (1) and (2) are only examples in Text 2.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'native' is followed by the preposition 'to': a plant or animal is native **to** the place it comes from.
'Native to Singapore, the Tembusu Tree can grow up to 40 metres tall.'
The answer is (N) to.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank is followed by 'who walk past'. We need a pronoun that stands for people and can take 'who'.
'those who ...' means 'the people who ...'. The plural verb 'walk' confirms a plural pronoun.
'some' cannot be used here because 'some who walk past' would mean only a few of them; the reminder is for everyone who walks past.
The answer is (M) those.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Pattern: such + a/an + adjective + singular noun ('such a tall tree').
The next word, 'iconic', begins with a vowel sound, so the article is 'an', not 'a'.
'Few would expect such an iconic image to be ... real'. The answer is (B) an.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank sits between 'also' and the adjective 'accessible', so it must be an adverb.
The tree on the five-dollar note is not just a drawing: it is real, and even today the public can go and see it. 'still' means 'even now'.
The answer is (L) still.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'the significance ___ the symbol': we need a preposition that links the meaning to the symbol.
We speak of the meaning, story or significance **behind** something, that is, the deeper meaning that lies under it.
The answer is (C) behind.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'is believed to have existed' is a perfect form, showing something that began in the past and has continued.
The blank is followed by a point in time: when 'the Botanic Gardens was officially founded in 1859'. From a starting point until now, we use 'since'.
'while' would mean only during that moment, which does not fit a tree that is close to two centuries old.
The answer is (J) since.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank comes 'been admired', so we need a helping verb to make the perfect passive: has/had + been + past participle.
The tree is still admired today ('some of whom return'), so use the present perfect. 'this tree' is singular: 'has'.
'had' would place the admiration wholly in the past. The answer is (F) has.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence begins with a phrase that describes what the tree possesses: 'its thick, weathered trunk and an expansive canopy of branches'.
'With + noun phrase' at the start of a sentence means 'having': With its thick trunk ..., the tree represents ...
'having' is the trap: 'Having its thick trunk ...' is not natural English, while 'With its ...' is the usual pattern.
The answer is (Q) with.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Two things are true at the same time: 'standing unshaken by storms' and 'remaining deeply grounded in its values'.
'while' joins two actions that go on together, and can be followed by a verb-ing form.
The answer is (P) while.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the dash, the sentence explains what Singapore takes pride **in**. A preposition ('in') is followed by a noun or a verb-ing form.
'anchored and forward-looking' are adjectives, so we need the -ing form of 'be' in front of them: 'being anchored and forward-looking'.
'having' does not work because we say someone **is** anchored, not **has** anchored.
The answer is (D) being.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++invovment++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The base word is 'involve' (in-volve). Add the suffix '-ment' without dropping the 'e': involve + ment.
Say it in syllables: in-volve-ment.
The correct word is 'involvement', which means taking part in something.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++litracy++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word comes from 'literate' (able to read and write).
Say it in four syllables so that no letter is lost: lit-er-a-cy. The unstressed 'e' is easy to miss.
The correct word is 'literacy'. 'Computer literacy' means knowing how to use computers.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++inntaitive++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word is linked to 'initial' and 'initiate' (to start something).
Spell it in parts: in-i-ti-a-tive. The 'sh' sound is spelt 'ti'.
The correct word is 'initiative', which here means a new plan or project.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++by++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong preposition.
A 'divide' is a gap that separates two groups. For two things we use 'between ... and ...': the divide between the young and old generations.
The correct word is 'between'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++emphatick++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Think about the meaning: volunteers who guide the elderly should understand how the elderly feel. That quality is 'empathy'.
The adjective from 'empathy' is 'empathetic': em-pa-thet-ic. It ends in '-ic', never '-ick'.
Do not confuse it with 'emphatic', which means said forcefully.
The correct word is 'empathetic'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++because++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong connector.

Look at the two ideas. It is easy for **us** to take the skill for granted. For **someone who did not grow up with digital technology**, it is intimidating. The two ideas contrast; the second is not the reason for the first.
A contrast needs 'but' (or 'yet'), not 'because'.
The correct word is 'but'.

review.note: 'yet' also shows the contrast and is accepted.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++those++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the pronoun does not agree with what it refers to.
The pronoun points back to 'such a skill set' or 'digital technology', each of which is one thing. 'those' is plural and is used for many things.
A singular pronoun is needed: 'this can be rather intimidating'. ('it' or 'that' is also singular and correct.)
The correct word is 'this'.

review.note: The key gives 'this'. Solved independently as 'it'; any singular pronoun ('this', 'it', 'that') corrects the error, so all three are accepted.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++applies++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the verb form.
'By' is a preposition, so the verbs after it take the -ing form: 'By sharing your knowledge and ___ your skills'.
The two verbs joined by 'and' must match (parallel structure): sharing ... and applying ...
The correct word is 'applying' (apply + ing; keep the 'y').

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++comunikation++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The base word is 'communicate', with double 'm' and a 'c' for the 'k' sound.
Drop the 'e' and add '-ion': com-mu-ni-ca-tion.
The correct word is 'communication'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++seen++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the verb form.
In 'look forward to', the word 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by a verb-ing form, not the base verb or the past participle.
'We look forward to seeing you at the workshop!'
The correct word is 'seeing'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: We need a noun for a person, described as 'an enthusiastic toy ___'.
Clue further on: he set up the museum with 'his personal collection from more than forty countries'. A person who has a collection is a collector.
The answer is 'collector'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'from all walks of life' is a fixed expression. It means people of every kind of job and background.
The words 'from all' before the blank and 'of life' after it are the clues.
The answer is 'walks'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: After the comma we need a verb-ing form that tells what the museum does with 'his personal collection'.
A museum puts things on show, so 'displaying' fits. The next paragraph confirms it: 'the museum **displays** toys from the 1840s'.
'showcasing', 'exhibiting' and 'featuring' have the same meaning and are also acceptable.
The answer is 'displaying'.

review.note: The key gives 'displaying'. Solved independently as 'showcasing', which has the same meaning; close synonyms are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'action figures, wind-up robots and miniature cars' are examples of toys.
To introduce examples after a noun we use 'like' ('such as' is two words, so it cannot be used).
The answer is 'like'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'children and adults alike' is a common pattern: 'A and B alike' means both A and B equally.
The toys awe (amaze) both groups in the same way.
The answer is 'alike'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: Clues: 'up with a key in the winding slot'. The verb is 'wind up' (to turn a key so that a toy can move).
The toys do not wind themselves; they are wound by someone. After 'when' we can use the past participle: 'when (they are) wound up'.
The past participle of 'wind' is 'wound', not 'winded'.
The answer is 'wound'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: Pattern: 'One of the + plural noun + singular verb'. Here: '___ of the highlights of the museum **is** the mechanical toy'.
The singular verb 'is' and the single item named ('the mechanical toy') show that just one highlight is meant.
The answer is 'One'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence lists three ways to power the toy, all in the -ing form: 'winding a key, ___ a button, or pushing a lever'. The missing verb must match (parallel structure).
The verb that goes with 'a button' is 'press'.
'pushing' is also possible for a button, but it is used for the lever straight after, so 'pressing' is the better choice.
The answer is 'pressing'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'instead of' means 'in place of'. The blank is followed by 'of relying on batteries'.
The toy is powered by hand (a key, a button, a lever) in place of batteries.
The answer is 'instead'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank comes after 'said the museum owner, his ___ carrying a note of nostalgia'.
'a note of' is used for the sound of feeling in someone's voice. What carries a note of nostalgia when a person speaks? His voice.
The answer is 'voice' ('tone' is also acceptable).

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'how toys had gradually evolved ___ the years': we need a preposition for a period of time during which a slow change happened.
'throughout the years' and 'over the years' both mean during the whole of that time.
The answer is 'throughout' ('over' is equally correct).

review.note: The key's word is partly under the watermark but reads 'throughout'. Solved independently as 'over'; both are standard and accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'It is indeed amazing to note ___ these toy characters were part of the children's playtime'.
After 'to note', a clause that states a fact is introduced by 'that'.
The answer is 'that'.

review.note: The key's word is partly under the watermark but reads 'that', matching the solved answer. 'how' is also accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: Think about the order of events: first children played with these toys; later technology (screens and gadgets) 'took over'.
The toys were part of playtime earlier than that, so the connector is 'before'.
The answer is 'before'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank is followed by 'to the past'. We need a base verb (after 'helps visitors') that takes 'to'.
Earlier the passage speaks of an 'emotional connection to the past'. To 'relate to' something is to feel a connection with it and understand it.
'connect to the past' has the same meaning and is also acceptable.
The answer is 'relate'.

review.note: The key gives 'relate'. Solved independently as 'connect' (the passage itself speaks of an 'emotional connection to the past'); both are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'come to life' is a fixed expression meaning to become lively, as if alive.
In the museum the toys move, make sounds and bring back memories, so the toys 'come to life'.
The answer is 'life'.

questions.stem:
Our relatives insisted on paying us a visit. It was raining heavily.
No matter how ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: No matter how heavily it was raining, our relatives insisted on paying us a visit.
accept: No matter how heavily it rained, our relatives insisted on paying us a visit.
No matter how heavily it was raining our relatives insisted on paying us a visit.
No matter how heavy the rain was, our relatives insisted on paying us a visit.
No matter how heavy the rain was our relatives insisted on paying us a visit.

explanation: 'No matter how' is followed straight away by an adjective or adverb, then the subject and verb: No matter how + heavily + it was raining.
Move 'heavily' forward so that it comes right after 'how'. Do not write 'No matter how it was raining heavily'.
Put a comma, then the main clause unchanged: 'our relatives insisted on paying us a visit'.
Keep the past tense. You may also change the adverb to an adjective with a noun: 'No matter how heavy the rain was, ...'.

review.keyAnswer: No matter how heavy the rain was our relatives insisted an [on] paying us a visit.
review.solvedAnswer: No matter how heavily it was raining, our relatives insisted on paying us a visit.
review.note: The key's version uses the adjective form ('how heavy the rain was') and has a typing slip ('insisted an'). The adverb form, which keeps the original words, is the model answer; both are accepted.

questions.stem:
The children do not like fried chicken wings. They like fruits and vegetables instead.
The children prefer ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: The children prefer fruits and vegetables to fried chicken wings.

explanation: Pattern: prefer + A (what is liked more) + **to** + B (what is liked less).
What they like goes first: fruits and vegetables. What they do not like goes after 'to': fried chicken wings.
Use 'to', not 'than'. 'prefer ... than' is a common mistake. ('rather than' is possible, but 'to' is the safest.)
Drop 'do not like' and 'instead', because 'prefer' already carries that meaning.

review.keyAnswer: The children prefer fruits and vegetable [vegetables] to fried chicken wings.
review.solvedAnswer: The children prefer fruits and vegetables to fried chicken wings.
review.note: The key is partly under the watermark; it reads 'fruits and vegetable to fried chicken wings', taken as a slip for 'vegetables'.

questions.stem:
"What is your decision after hearing all the available options?" my mother asked me.
My mother asked me ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: My mother asked me what my decision was after hearing all the available options.

explanation: This is a reported question. Keep the question word 'what', but change the question word order to statement order: subject first, then verb ('what my decision was', not 'what was my decision').
Change the pronoun to fit the speaker: 'your decision' becomes 'my decision'.
The reporting verb 'asked' is in the past, so move the tense back: 'is' becomes 'was'.
End with a full stop, not a question mark, and remove the quotation marks.

review.keyAnswer: My mother asked me what my decision was after hearing all the available options.
review.solvedAnswer: My mother asked me what my decision was after hearing all the available options.
review.note: The key is partly under the watermark but readable.

questions.stem:
The team members were sorry about not running faster during the final event.
The team members wished that ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: The team members wished that they had run faster during the final event.

explanation: A wish about the past (a regret) uses: wished + (that) + subject + **had + past participle**.
They regret 'not running faster', so they wished the opposite had happened: they had run faster. Remove 'not'.
The past participle of 'run' is 'run' (run, ran, run): 'had run', not 'had ran'.
Use 'they' for the team members and keep 'during the final event'.

review.keyAnswer: The team members wished that they had run faster during the final event.
review.solvedAnswer: The team members wished that they had run faster during the final event.

questions.stem:
The lifts are maintained regularly to ensure that they function properly.
The regular ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: The regular maintenance of the lifts ensures that they function properly.
accept: The regular maintenance of the lifts is to ensure that they function properly.
The regular maintenance of the lifts ensures they function properly.

explanation: 'The regular' must be followed by a noun, so change the verb 'maintained' to its noun form 'maintenance' (spelling: main-ten-ance). The adverb 'regularly' has become the adjective 'regular'.
Say what is maintained with 'of': 'The regular maintenance of the lifts'.
The subject is now 'maintenance', which is singular, so the verb is 'ensures' (not 'ensure').
Keep the rest: 'that they function properly'.

review.keyAnswer: The regular maintenance of the lifts ensures that they function properly.
review.solvedAnswer: The regular maintenance of the lifts ensures that they function properly.

questions.stem: We can infer that the writer did not like his performance outfit. Give two reasons why he felt that way.

parts.label: a

answer.value: The rabbit costume was garish, with neon pink fur.

explanation: Find the description of the costume in paragraph 1: 'not the soft, storybook kind, but a garish ensemble of neon pink fur with ears that drooped like they had given up hope. Its oversized head sagged to one side.'
Each unattractive feature is one reason. First: it was garish (unpleasantly bright), made of neon pink fur.

Other acceptable reasons from the same lines: its ears drooped; its oversized head sagged to one side; it looked less presentable than everyone else's outfit. Give two different reasons, one on each line.

parts.label: b

answer.value: Its head was oversized and sagged to one side.

explanation: The second reason must be a different feature from the first.
'Its oversized head sagged to one side.' The head was too big and lopsided, so the costume looked silly.
You could also write that its ears drooped, or that everyone else's outfit 'looked far more presentable' than his.

review.keyAnswer: a) The rabbit costume had he [had neon] pink fur. b) The head of the rabbit costume was oversized.
review.solvedAnswer: Garish neon pink fur; drooping ears; oversized head that sagged; less presentable than the others' outfits. Agrees with key.
review.note: The key's (a) reads 'had he on pink fur', taken as a slip for 'had neon pink fur'. Any two of the unattractive features in lines 3 to 8 should earn the marks.

questions.stem: Besides having to wear the costume, state two other reasons for the writer's anxiety about the performance.

parts.label: a

answer.value: It was his debut performance, so he was worried about making a mistake.

explanation: Leave the costume out; the question says 'besides'. Look for what else made the event feel frightening.

Paragraph 1: 'This was it. My debut performance. My graduation day.' A debut is a first performance. He had never performed before, so he feared failing: in paragraph 3 he stumbles over a line and asks himself, 'was that failure?'
Key idea: it was his first time performing and he was afraid of making mistakes or failing.

parts.label: b

answer.value: There would be an expectant audience watching, and he was worried that they would laugh at him.

explanation: Paragraph 1: 'A room with an expectant audience...'. Many people would be watching and expecting a good show.

His fear of the audience is shown later: at the rehearsal the giggles spread 'like wildfire', and on opening night he is relieved that the laughter was 'not mockery' and that he 'was not being laughed at'.
Key idea: he was afraid of being laughed at by the audience.

review.keyAnswer: a) The writer was worried about making a mistake. b) The writer was worried about the audience laughing at him.
review.solvedAnswer: It was his debut (first) performance on his graduation day; there would be an expectant audience.
review.note: The key names the fears (making a mistake; being laughed at). Solved independently from lines 5 to 6 as the causes (it was his debut performance; an expectant audience would be watching). These are the same two ideas seen from different sides, so the model answer combines them; either wording should be accepted when self-marking.

questions.stem: Fill in each blank with **a word** that **best** describes the writer's feelings.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
"A room with an expectant audience... and that was what I had to wear?" (lines 5–6, paragraph 1)
This tells me that the writer was afraid of being ____________________.
explanation: The writer pictures a room full of people looking at him in a costume he finds awful. The italics show his disbelief.
What does a person fear when he must look silly in front of a crowd? Being embarrassed, or being laughed at (ridiculed, mocked).
One word only. The answer is 'embarrassed' ('ridiculed', 'mocked' or 'humiliated' carry the same idea).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
"Somehow, everyone's outfit looked far more presentable than mine." (line 8, paragraph 1)
This tells me that the writer was ____________________ of his classmates' costumes.
explanation: He compares his costume with the others' and finds theirs 'far more presentable'. He wishes he had what they have.
Wanting what someone else has is being jealous or envious. Both words are followed by 'of', which fits the blank.
The answer is 'jealous' (or 'envious').

review.solvedAnswer: a) ridiculed / embarrassed b) envious / jealous

questions.stem: Fill in the following table by identifying the correct words or sentence from lines 10–18 (paragraph 2).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which five-word phrase tells us that Leon did not mind his costume?
explanation: Find Leon's costume in paragraph 2: he was 'fiddling with the long frayed tail of his goat costume, looking as ridiculous as I felt, **yet standing tall all the same**'.
To 'stand tall' is to carry yourself proudly and confidently. 'all the same' means 'anyway'. So he looked ridiculous but was not bothered.
Count exactly five words: standing (1) tall (2) all (3) the (4) same (5). Leave out 'yet', which would make six.
The answer is 'standing tall all the same'.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Which sentence suggests that teamwork was valued?

accept: We are all in this together

explanation: Look in Leon's speech for words about the group rather than one person.
'We're all in this together.' The words 'we', 'all' and 'together' show that everyone shares the task and supports one another. That is teamwork.
Copy the whole sentence exactly, and only that sentence.
The answer is 'We're all in this together.'

review.keyAnswer: a) standing tall all the same b) we're all in his [this] together.
review.solvedAnswer: a) standing tall all the same b) We're all in this together.
review.note: The key's (b) has a typing slip ('in his together').

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the words in the left column refer to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a

answer.value: The costumes hanging in the closet, including the costumes that the writer's classmates would be wearing.

explanation: 'Taking in the **scene**, I noticed the others – fluffy sheep, dignified goats, even cows'.
A 'scene' is a view, what you see in front of you. The writer had just opened the closet door, so the scene is what was inside: his rabbit costume and the other costumes hanging there.
'the others' are the other costumes, the ones his classmates would wear.
The answer is the sight of the costumes in the closet (the costumes that the writer and his classmates had to wear).

parts.label: b

answer.value: The long rehearsals, the endless retakes and the body aches.

explanation: 'The long rehearsals, the endless retakes, the body aches. Had I forgotten all **those**?'
'those' is plural and points back to the list in the sentence just before it.
Name all three things: the long rehearsals, the endless retakes and the body aches. Together they are the hard work he had put in.

parts.label: c

answer.value: Wearing the rabbit costume to perform on stage.
accept: wearing the rabbit costume to perform
performing on stage in the rabbit costume

explanation: 'Thanks for talking me out of leaving. **It** isn't so bad after all,' I replied, tugging at the floppy ears.
He tugs at the costume's ears as he speaks and goes on to say 'This outfit still looks ridiculous.' So 'It' is the thing he had dreaded and wanted to run away from: performing in the rabbit costume.
Test by replacing: 'Performing in the rabbit costume isn't so bad after all.' It makes sense.
The answer is wearing the rabbit costume to perform.

review.keyAnswer: a) The costume that the writer's classmates were wearing. b) The long rehearsals, the endless takes [retakes] and the body aches. c) Weaving [Wearing] the rabbit costume to perform.
review.solvedAnswer: a) what he saw in the closet: the costumes hanging there; b) the long rehearsals, endless retakes and body aches; c) performing in the rabbit costume.
review.note: For (a) the key limits 'scene' to the classmates' costumes; the model answer is slightly wider (all the costumes in the closet), which includes the key's answer. The key has typing slips in (b) 'takes' and (c) 'Weaving'. Only the three words asked about (scene, those, It) are bold in the passage, plus the sentence quoted in Q71.

questions.stem: "Lying there, humiliation scorched my face." (line 28, paragraph 3). What made the writer feel that way?

answer.value: When the writer was exiting the stage after his part, his oversized foot caught on a mess of wires and he tripped and landed on his knees, and the audience burst into laughter.

explanation: Read the sentences just before the quotation: 'Exiting the stage after my part, my oversized foot caught on a mess of wires. Like a puppet with its strings cut, I tripped and landed on my knees. Laughter exploded.'
'Lying there' tells us he had fallen. 'Humiliation' is deep embarrassment, and it came from people laughing at his fall.
The marker looks for both ideas: he tripped (over the wires) and fell, and everyone laughed at him.

review.keyAnswer: When the writer was exiting the stage after his part his oversized foot caught on a mess of wires, causing him to trip and land on his knees. The audience started laughing.
review.solvedAnswer: He tripped over the wires, landed on his knees and everyone laughed. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on lines 19–36 (paragraphs 3 and 4), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Initially, the laughter during the practice session made the writer want to give up acting.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. When the laughter spread, the writer doubted himself and thought that if there were a trapdoor, he would gladly vanish.

explanation: The 'practice session' is the full-dress rehearsal in paragraph 3. Find what the laughter did to him.
'Laughter. More laughter. The gnawing doubt clawed at me – was that failure? What a disaster! If there were a trapdoor, I would gladly vanish.'
Wanting to disappear through a trapdoor shows that he wanted to get off the stage and give up. So the statement is True.
'Initially' matters: later in the paragraph he changed his mind and decided to face his fears.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
On the performance night, the writer was not mentally prepared.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. His stomach churned with butterflies, but this time he welcomed them.

explanation: The performance night is the opening night in paragraph 4.
'My stomach churned with butterflies, but this time, I welcomed them.' He was still nervous, but he accepted the feeling instead of fearing it.
Welcoming his nerves shows that he was mentally ready. So the statement is False.
Further support: 'The fears were irrational. I had made peace with them.'

review.keyAnswer: a) True / The writer felt humiliated and he would have gladly vanished if there had been a trapdoor. b) False / The writer was mentally prepared. His stomach churned with butterflies but he welcomed them.
review.solvedAnswer: a) True: doubt clawed at him and he wished he could vanish through a trapdoor. b) False: he welcomed the butterflies this time. Agrees with key.
review.note: In line 25 the scan shows 'I would gladly vanished' with the 'ed' struck out by hand; the passage is transcribed with the corrected 'vanish'.

questions.stem: Referring to lines 19–30 (paragraph 3), what made the writer change his mindset about facing his fears?

answer.value: As he lay on the floor feeling humiliated after tripping, the writer remembered Leon's words, "We all start somewhere." They made him realise that even though people had laughed at him, he had to face his fears instead of running away.

explanation: Find the turning point near the end of paragraph 3: 'All of a sudden, something changed. I remembered Leon's words. "We all start somewhere." I knew I had to face my fears.'
What caused the change (1 mark): he remembered Leon's words, 'We all start somewhere.'
What he then understood (1 mark): everyone is a beginner at first, so stumbling and being laughed at are normal, and he had to face his fears rather than run from them.
Quote Leon's words exactly and explain what they made him realise.

review.keyAnswer: The writer remembered Leon's words "We all start somewhere". The writer realised that even though the audience laughed at him, he should still face his fears.
review.solvedAnswer: He remembered Leon's words 'We all start somewhere' and knew he had to face his fears. Agrees with key.
review.note: The second half of the key's answer is under the watermark but readable.

questions.stem: Complete the table below. What is the purpose for each of the characters' actions?

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Writer: made silly twitches on the rabbit's ears

answer.value: To make the audience laugh and add to their enjoyment of the show.

explanation: Paragraph 4: 'Every exaggerated movement, every silly twitch of my ears added to the joy ... my antics were making the guests laugh.'
'antics' are funny, playful actions. He twitched the ears on purpose to amuse the audience.
The purpose: to make the audience laugh (to entertain them).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Leon: gave the writer a thumbs-up

answer.value: To encourage the writer and show him that he was doing well (putting on a good show).

explanation: Paragraph 4: 'Backstage, Leon flashed me a thumbs-up.'
A thumbs-up is a sign of approval. Leon gave it while the writer was performing well, and afterwards said, 'You did it! You're a natural.'
The purpose: to praise and encourage the writer, to show that he was doing a good job.

review.keyAnswer: To make the audience laugh. / For putting on a good show.
review.solvedAnswer: Writer: to make the audience laugh. Leon: to encourage him and show approval of his performance. Agrees with key.
review.note: The key's first line is under the watermark but readable. Its second line, 'For putting on a good show', is a reason rather than a purpose; the model answer rewrites it as a purpose (to praise or encourage the writer).

questions.stem: What doubt did the writer have in the beginning and how had this attitude changed after the performance?

answer.value: In the beginning, the writer doubted that he could perform in his ridiculous costume without being laughed at, and he wanted to slip away. After the performance, he felt it was a success: he had learnt about courage and that the stage was not about perfection but about showing up, even when he was scared.

explanation: This needs two parts: the doubt at the start (1 mark) and the changed attitude at the end (1 mark).

Beginning (paragraph 1): his heart sank when he saw the costume, he feared facing 'an expectant audience' in it, and 'had the urge to slip away'. He doubted he could perform well and worried that people would laugh at him.

After the performance (paragraph 6): 'It isn't so bad after all ... I had learnt about courage and that the stage was not about perfection. It was about showing up, even when I was scared. My debut performance was a success.'
Use signal words such as 'In the beginning' and 'After the performance' so that the marker can see both parts.

review.keyAnswer: In the beginning, the writer was worried that people would laugh at him. After the performance, the writer thought that the performance was a success and that he had learnt about courage and that the stage was not about perfection.
review.solvedAnswer: At first he doubted he could go on stage in the ridiculous costume without being laughed at; afterwards he saw the performance as a success and learnt that the stage is about courage and showing up, not perfection. Agrees with key.
review.note: The last two lines of the key's answer are under the watermark but readable.
